judged_text: evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars) is called when evt.destinationCalendar was just set to null three lines above (when neither eventType.destinationCalendar nor organizerUser.destinationCalendar exists), so it calls push on null and throws. Every COLLECTIVE booking where the event type and organizer have no destination calendar fails with 'Cannot read properties of null (reading push)' — a 500 on the booking endpoint for a common configuration, not an edge case.

adjudication.rationale: In `handleNewBooking.ts`, `evt.destinationCalendar` can be set to `null` (`... : null`), but the subsequent call is `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars);` which uses optional chaining. Optional chaining safely short-circuits on `null`/`undefined`, so `push` is not invoked and no `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'push')` error would be thrown from this line as shown in the diff.
